title: Search Engine Journal: most ways of measuring AI presence are untested (6 Nov 2026)
why: The article argues dashboard AI-presence scores should be tested against customer behavior; our readiness score answers a different question and we should say so.

drafts.text: A dashboard that scores AI presence and a readiness score answer different questions. Ours reads robots.txt, llms.txt and the homepage. It never asks an assistant whether it names a brand. Report the two numbers separately.

Most AI presence dashboards answer one question: what do assistants say about us. A readiness score answers a different one: can crawlers reach the site, and do its pages carry signals a model can read.

I build the second kind, so I have a bias here. The scan reads robots.txt, llms.txt, the sitemap and the homepage. It gives a 100-point score from 16 checks, plus the access state of 10 AI crawlers. It never asks an assistant whether it names a brand, so I would not read that number as presence.

If your team reports both, put them on separate lines with separate labels. A higher readiness score tells you the door is open. It does not tell you anyone walked through it.

Method note: this is a reading of one Search Engine Journal article dated 6 Nov 2026, not a test. The score measures readiness only. It is not a citation or ranking measure.
